_doc: Use cases on /for-organisations. No client or partner is named. Public cards link to open pages. Private cards carry findings only; every figure was checked against the work's own verified ledger or raw source file on 14 Oct 2026, and the source and edition behind each is named here.

public.question: Is this factory’s water secure?
public.did: A site water reading for a food factory: the groundwater status of its taluk, the tanks around it and the rules on drawing groundwater. The district view it rests on is open.
public.finding: In July 2026 the 42 registered tanks around the site held 21 ha of water, 4% of their 486 ha and the second-lowest July since 2020.
public.findingSources: The state tank register with monthly satellite water readings, July 2020 to July 2026
public.imageAlt: The Kolar district page on Neer Vazhvu, showing all six taluks over-exploited or critical for groundwater.

public.question: What does this canal look like today, kilometre by kilometre?
public.did: A baseline of the Buckingham Canal from Ennore to Mahabalipuram: its course, the width of open water every fifty metres, and how its banks have changed.
public.imageAlt: The Buckingham Canal page on Neer Vazhvu, measured from Ennore to Mahabalipuram fifty metres at a time.

public.question: What runs through this district’s rivers, and who draws on them?
public.did: A district river atlas joining rivers, canals, reservoirs, groundwater, sewage outfalls and industry, down to each village panchayat.
public.imageAlt: The Erode district river map on Neer Vazhvu, with rivers, canals and sub-basins drawn over the district.

public.question: Can a city’s rivers, lakes and supply lakes sit on one map?
public.did: A rivers-and-lakes atlas for Mumbai, built with a local partner: river catchments, the seven supply lakes, polluted stretches, flood spots and treatment plants.
public.imageAlt: The Mumbai rivers and lakes map on Neer Vazhvu, with the rivers and supply lakes drawn across the region.

private.question: Which lakes should restoration money go to next?
private.finding: Of the 210 lakes on Greater Bengaluru’s custody lists, 180 were read the same way and placed in classes a funder can act on: 23 need attention, 15 are ready to co-fund and 44 need design first. The next edition follows in November 2026.
private.findingSources: Custody lists of Greater Bengaluru’s lake agencies; Sentinel-2, 28 March 2017 to 30 August 2026

private.question: Did the restoration hold water?
private.figureLabel: of water at Jakkur every year, 2012–2021
private.finding: Before its 2008–12 works Jakkur held 15 to 38 ha of water a year; since, 35 to 38 ha every year. Kaikondrahalli never held more than 8 ha before 2010 and has held 7 to 11 ha every year since its restoration. Every year from 2018 to 2026, a typical clear image showed signs of algae across the open water of all three lakes we read.
private.findingSources: EC JRC Global Surface Water (Landsat), 1988–2021; Sentinel-2, 2017 to October 2026

private.question: How much groundwater is left under this industrial area?
private.figureLabel: of its sustainable groundwater drawn by the block, 2024–25
private.finding: All 14 of Alwar’s blocks are over-exploited in every assessment from 2021–22 to 2024–25, and the district draws 182.1% of what can be drawn sustainably. The block holding an industrial area near Alwar city draws 211.8%.

private.question: Which streets flood, and how much do blocked drains add?
private.figureLabel: working, half-blocked and blocked, in a storm like 5 September 2022
private.finding: A street-scale model of one neighbourhood’s low ground and drains shows standing water spreading further at every step from working to blocked drains. We map where water spreads, never how deep it stands.
private.findingSources: Terrain, drain and rainfall scenarios for HSR Layout
